detail.longDescription: I have a method decorated with @property : class Foo: @property def prop(self): pass It prevents modification and deletion, as intended: f = Foo() f.prop = 1 # AttributeError: property 'prop' of 'Foo' object has no setter del f.prop # AttributeError: property 'prop' of 'Foo' object has no deleter Since in my case prop is expensive, I want to cache it. @cached_property is built for this very purpose: from functools import cached_property class Foo: @cached_property def prop(self): pass But it allows setting and deleting the attribute: f = Foo() f.prop = 1 # no error del f.prop # no error How can I cache an @property similarly to @cached_property while preventing setting and deleting the attribute? A MRE for reference: import traceback from functools import cached_property class Foo: @property def a(self) -> int: '@property' return 42 @cached_property def b(self) -> int: '@cached_property' return 42 f = Foo() for attr in 'a', 'b': prop = getattr(Foo, attr) print('setattr on', prop.__doc__) try: setattr(f, attr, 24) except AttributeError: print() traceback.print_exc() print() print('delattr on', prop.__doc__) try: delattr(f, attr) except AttributeError: print() traceback.print_exc() print() print('===================') print() Output: setattr on @property Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\CHU0094\Downloads\x\test.py", line 22, in <module> setattr(f, attr, 24) ~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: property 'a' of 'Foo' object has no setter delattr on @property Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\CHU0094\Downloads\x\test.py", line 31, in <module> delattr(f, attr) ~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: property 'a' of 'Foo' object has no deleter =================== setattr on @cached_property delattr on @cached_property
